short: Nine months on the throne, two invasions, and the end of Anglo-Saxon England.
full:
Harold Godwinson was crowned on 6 January 1066, the day after Edward the Confessor died and probably in accordance with the dying king's nomination. He was the most powerful earl in England but had no royal blood, and both William of Normandy and Harald Hardrada of Norway claimed the throne against him.

He spent the summer waiting on the south coast with the fleet and the fyrd. Supplies ran out in early September and the levy went home; Hardrada landed in Yorkshire days later. Harold marched north, destroyed the Norwegian army at Stamford Bridge on 25 September, then turned round and covered some 250 miles back to Sussex in under three weeks. On 14 October he met William near Hastings and was killed there with both his brothers. No Anglo-Saxon claimant was crowned again, and within a generation the English landholding class had been almost entirely replaced.
